hook.en: [NiCl₄]²⁻ is pulled by a magnet but [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻ is not, though both contain Ni²⁺. *Valence bond theory* explains this through hybridisation.
hook.kn: [NiCl₄]²⁻ ಕಾಂತಕ್ಕೆ ಆಕರ್ಷಿತವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ, [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻ ಆಗುವುದಿಲ್ಲ; ಎರಡರಲ್ಲೂ Ni²⁺ ಇದೆ. ವೇಲೆನ್ಸ್ ಬಂಧ ಸಿದ್ಧಾಂತ ಇದನ್ನು ಸಂಕರಣದ ಮೂಲಕ ವಿವರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: [NiCl 4] squared⁻ is pulled by a magnet but [NiCN 4] squared⁻ is not, though both contain Ni squared⁺. Valence bond theory explains this through hybridisation. In this lesson: Predict hybridisation and shape from VBT.
Distinguish inner and outer orbital complexes.
Use magnetic data to decide the bonding.

body.en: In VBT, the metal ion uses empty hybrid orbitals to accept lone pairs from the ligands. CN 4: sp³ (tetrahedral) or dsp² (square planar). CN 6: d²sp³, using inner (n−1)d orbitals, or sp³d², using outer nd orbitals; both are octahedral. Strong ligands such as CN⁻ and NH₃ (with Co³⁺) often pair up d electrons to free inner d orbitals, giving low-spin inner orbital *complexes*. Weak ligands such as F⁻ and H₂O leave the electrons unpaired, giving high-spin outer orbital complexes.
body.kn: ವೇಲೆನ್ಸ್ ಬಂಧ ಸಿದ್ಧಾಂತದಲ್ಲಿ ಲೋಹ ಅಯಾನು ಖಾಲಿ ಸಂಕರ ಕಕ್ಷೆಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಲಿಗ್ಯಾಂಡ್‌ಗಳ ಇಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್ ಜೋಡಿಗಳನ್ನು ಸ್ವೀಕರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. sp³ ಚತುಷ್ಫಲಕೀಯ, dsp² ಸಮತಲ ಚೌಕ, d²sp³ ಮತ್ತು sp³d² ಅಷ್ಟಫಲಕೀಯ.

say.en: In VBT, the metal ion uses empty hybrid orbitals to accept lone pairs from the ligands. CN 4: sp cubed tetrahedral or dsp squared square planar. CN 6: d squaredsp cubed, using inner (n-1)d orbitals, or sp cubedd squared, using outer nd orbitals; both are octahedral. Strong ligands such as CN⁻ and NH 3 (with Co cubed⁺) often pair up d electrons to free inner d orbitals, giving low-spin inner orbital complexes. Weak ligands such as F⁻ and H 2O leave the electrons unpaired, giving high-spin outer orbital complexes. sp cubed: tetrahedral; dsp squared: square planar.

say.en: d squaredsp cubed: inner orbital, low spin.
sp cubedd squared: outer orbital, high spin.

title.en: On the board: valence bond theory

say.en: Cobalt three plus is d six. Ammonia pairs up the d electrons, leaving two inner d orbitals for d2sp3 hybridisation: low spin and diamagnetic.
Fluoride is a weak ligand. The four unpaired d electrons stay, and the outer 4d orbitals are used: sp3d2, high spin, paramagnetic.
Nickel two plus is d eight. Cyanide pairs the electrons, giving dsp2 and a square planar, diamagnetic ion. Chloride does not, giving sp3, tetrahedral, two unpaired.
The spin-only formula turns unpaired electrons into the magnetic moment. Hexacyanidoferrate three has one unpaired electron: 1.73 BM.

narration.en: Set the number of 3d electrons of the metal ion. A strong-field ligand such as CN⁻ pairs the electrons up to free two 3d orbitals for d²sp³ bonding (inner orbital, low spin); a weak-field ligand such as F⁻ uses 4d orbitals (sp³d², outer orbital, high spin).

body.en: Measuring the *magnetic* moment tells us the number of unpaired electrons and so the hybridisation. [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ is diamagnetic: d²sp³. [CoF₆]³⁻ has four unpaired electrons: sp³d². [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻ is diamagnetic: dsp². [NiCl₄]²⁻ has two unpaired electrons: sp³. VBT has limits: it is qualitative, it does not explain colour, it cannot predict whether a complex will be inner or outer orbital without magnetic data, and it does not distinguish weak and strong ligands.
body.kn: ಕಾಂತೀಯ ಭ್ರಾಮಕದಿಂದ ಜೋಡಿಯಾಗದ ಇಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನುಗಳ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆ ಮತ್ತು ಸಂಕರಣ ತಿಳಿಯುತ್ತದೆ. ವೇಲೆನ್ಸ್ ಬಂಧ ಸಿದ್ಧಾಂತ ಬಣ್ಣವನ್ನು ವಿವರಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ ಮತ್ತು ಪ್ರಬಲ–ದುರ್ಬಲ ಲಿಗ್ಯಾಂಡ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು ಪ್ರತ್ಯೇಕಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.

narration.en: Spin-only magnetic moment against the number of unpaired electrons. Measuring μ tells us how many electrons are unpaired, and so the hybridisation. [CoF₆]³⁻ has 4 unpaired electrons: 4.90 BM. [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ is diamagnetic: n = 0. [NiCl₄]²⁻: n = 2, 2.83 BM.

say.en: Spin-only magnetic moment against the number of unpaired electrons. Measuring micro tells us how many electrons are unpaired, and so the hybridisation. [CoF 6] cubed⁻ has 4 unpaired electrons: 4.90 BM. [CoNH 3 6] cubed⁺ is diamagnetic: n equals 0. [NiCl 4] squared⁻: n equals 2, 2.83 BM.

problem.en: Using VBT, find the hybridisation, shape and magnetic moment of [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻.

steps.en: Fe³⁺ = 3d⁵ (5 unpaired). Strong-field CN⁻ pairs them into three 3d orbitals: 2 pairs + 1 unpaired.
Two empty 3d, one 4s and three 4p orbitals form d²sp³ hybrids: octahedral, inner orbital.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Using VBT, find the hybridisation, shape and magnetic moment of [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Using VBT, find the hybridisation, shape and magnetic moment of [FeCN 6] cubed⁻.
Fe cubed⁺ = 3d to the power 5 5 unpaired. Strong-field CN⁻ pairs them into three 3d orbitals: 2 pairs plus 1 unpaired.
Two empty 3d, one 4 seconds and three 4p orbitals form d squaredsp cubed hybrids: octahedral, inner orbital.
n equals 1: micro equals the square root of 1 times 3 equals 1.73 BM, paramagnetic.
So the answer is d squaredsp cubed, octahedral, 1.73 BM.

problem.en: Find the hybridisation and magnetic moment of [CoF₆]³⁻.

steps.en: Co³⁺ = 3d⁶. Weak-field F⁻ does not pair the electrons: one pair + 4 unpaired.
No inner d orbital is free, so 4s, 4p and two 4d orbitals give sp³d²: outer orbital, octahedral.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Find the hybridisation and magnetic moment of [CoF₆]³⁻.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Find the hybridisation and magnetic moment of [CoF 6] cubed⁻.
Co cubed⁺ = 3d to the power 6. Weak-field F⁻ does not pair the electrons: one pair plus 4 unpaired.
No inner d orbital is free, so 4 seconds, 4p and two 4d orbitals give sp cubedd squared: outer orbital, octahedral.
micro equals the square root of 4 times 6 equals the square root of 24 equals 4.90 BM.
So the answer is sp cubedd squared, octahedral, 4.90 BM.
